# Results — Study 686 (Stick Sandwich)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim (Nison,
*Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques*) — **a bullish stick sandwich (a bearish candle, a
bullish candle that rallies above it, then a second bearish candle that gives the whole rally
back and closes at ~the same level as the first) marks a support level tested twice, and calls
a bottom** — encoded as a mechanical rule. A sandwich completes at bar *t* when there is a
confirmed 10-day down leg into the pattern, candle *t-2* is **bearish**, candle *t-1* is
**bullish** and closes *above* candle *t-2*, candle *t* is **bearish**, and the two bearish
closes **meet** (`|close[t] − close[t-2]| / close[t-2] ≤ 15 bps`). A long fires on the
sandwich bar's close, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the
forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) OHLC for **SPY + 29 long-listed US large-caps** (public, no key) — the same "large basket" convention as sibling study [685-tri-star-doji](../685-tri-star-doji/) |
| Window | 2001-07-10 → 2026-06-30 (**As-of 2026-06-30**, partial July dropped; **~25.0** years/name, 188,400 total bars) |
| SPY fingerprint | `26d2248068a7` (content hash of the As-of-sliced OHLC) |
| Panel fingerprint | `3e40346f84dd` (sha1 over every name's close column, ticker-sorted) |
| Entries | **873** mechanical stick sandwiches pooled across the 30 names (tol = 15 bps, 10-day down-leg context); per-name count ranges **14 → 43** |
| Timing / costs | down leg + bearish/bullish-rally/bearish + equal close read on bar *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **5 bp** one-way × 2 legs per signal |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The tickers are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) —
> labelled total-return everywhere. This is a pooled single-instrument pattern study (not a
> cross-sectional anomaly), so survivorship (long-listed large-caps) affects mainly the
> unconditional drift baseline — which is exactly what the base-rate control below
> neutralizes, since it is measured on the *same* survivors.

## The signal — sandwich vs the unconditional base rate (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the basket's upward drift, inherited
by any long); the **Welch sandwich-vs-base-rate** *t* is the test that matters. Base rate = the
same long, entered the next close, on **every** eligible bar of the same 30-name panel. Because
four horizons are four simultaneous looks at one question, the certifying bar is the
**Bonferroni-corrected** critical value for *k* = 4: **|t| ≥ 2.50** (not the naive 2.00).

| horizon | n | sandwich | win% | one-sample *t* | base rate | Δ (sandwich−base) | net of cost | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 873 | +38.4 bps  | 55% | +3.09 | +26.9 bps  | **+11.5 bps** | +28.4 bps  | +1.01 |
| 10-day | 873 | +50.5 bps  | 57% | +3.16 | +53.4 bps  | **−2.9 bps**  | +40.5 bps  | −0.19 |
| 20-day | 871 | +99.3 bps  | 58% | +4.29 | +106.6 bps | **−7.3 bps**  | +89.3 bps  | −0.33 |
| 60-day | 865 | +327.1 bps | 65% | +7.55 | +321.9 bps | **+5.2 bps**  | +317.1 bps | +0.14 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks respectable and grows with the
horizon (**+3.09 → +7.55**) — but that is **pure beta**: a long-only entry on an upward-drifting
30-name large-cap basket inherits the basket's drift, pattern or no pattern. Against the
**drift-matched base rate**, the sandwich adds essentially nothing at any horizon: the
sandwich-minus-base delta swings from −7.3 to +11.5 bps with no consistent sign, and the
Welch *t* **never clears 2**, let alone the Bonferroni bar of 2.50 (max |*t*| = 1.01, at 5
days). The pattern does not forecast the bounce it claims.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the equal close, keep the failed-rally context

The decisive "does the *equal close* matter?" test: keep the down-leg +
bearish/bullish-rally/bearish context (the "almost-sandwich" candidates) but **ignore the
equal-close test**, drawing the same number of entries at random from that candidate pool. If
price genuinely respected the *matching closes* (not just "a rally that failed after a down
leg"), the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | context-matched candidates | observed sandwich 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY equal-close scramble | 232 | +243.6 bps | **0.110** | 1,000 |

**~11% of context-matched, no-equal-close draws match or beat the real sandwich** (*p* =
0.110). That is above the conventional 0.05 bar — the defining "closes meet twice" geometry is
**not shown to be load-bearing**: a plain failed rally after a 10-day decline does nearly as
well, whether or not the two bearish candles actually land at the same price.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic panel with a *planted* post-sandwich reversal (knob `edge`), the same
Welch sandwich-vs-base-rate detector behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result
is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.31** (sd 0.90), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = 1.00 (seed 686, 606 planted sandwiches) | **+23.08** (sandwich +702.7 bps vs base +236.0 bps) |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up hard on a planted bounce.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The stick sandwich does **not** beat the drift-matched unconditional base
  rate: the sandwich-minus-base Welch *t* is **+1.01 / −0.19 / −0.33 / +0.14** at 5/10/20/60
  days — nowhere near the naive |*t*| ≥ 2 bar, let alone the **Bonferroni-corrected 2.50** bar
  for four simultaneous horizon tests. The respectable one-sample *t*'s (up to +7.55 at 60
  days) are **pure beta** — the basket's upward drift, which any long-only entry rides for
  free.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No residual edge once the free drift is removed; at two of the
  four horizons the pattern is already a net negative before costs, and 10 bps of round-trip
  cost only deepens the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply by holding the basket.
- **"Does the equal-close 'meeting' add anything beyond a plain failed rally?" — BUSTED.** The
  equal-close scramble placebo leaves the result essentially intact (*p* = 0.110): context-
  matched candidates that ignore the equal-close condition do about as well as the real
  sandwiches. The defining "two matching closes" geometry carries no detectable extra
  information — the stick sandwich is a descriptive label for a failed bounce after a
  decline, not a forecasting signal.
